messages:
alex (oncall): FYI alert from SIEM: high rate of kms:GenerateDataKey for service-account 'analytics-worker@prod'. spike started ~00:12 UTC, ~180 requests in 3m. suspicious. tagging incident.

jordan-sec: on it. do we have an active deploy or rollout that could explain this?

alex (oncall): checked deploy-bot, no deployments in the window. request IPs are from us-east-1 lambda pool but a single container ID looks odd. attaching sample audit line below.

alex (oncall): ```json
{ "eventTime":"2026-03-20T00:12:23Z", "principal":"svc-analytics@redwood-prod", "action":"kms:GenerateDataKey", "keyId":"alias/services-data-prod", "srcIp":"54.210.12.45" }
```

maria-sre: +1 treat as potential compromised service account until proven otherwise. immediate actions: 1) revoke service-account tokens, 2) rotate key material for alias/services-data-prod (create new key or rekey), 3) snapshot audit logs to immutable storage. who can rotate keys now?

samir-engr: I can revoke the service account token via IAM. doing it now: `gcloud iam service-accounts disable svc-analytics@redwood-prod` (running).

carla-enginfra: I will create a KMS key rotation plan. prefer to create a new key and re-encrypt only recent blobs to avoid mass re-encrypt. initiating key creation (kms-cli create-key --alias services-data-prod-v2)

jordan-sec: hold on rotation until we capture evidence — need to preserve original key usage for forensic. Instead: disable the service account + limit its roles and add deny policy for GenerateDataKey, then snapshot logs. After that we can schedule rekey.

maria-sre: agreed. alex, can you export the CloudTrail/Stackdriver events for keyId alias/services-data-prod for the 12:00-00:20 window to the secure S3 bucket (s3://incidents/1812349999)? mark as immutable.

alex (oncall): exporting now: `aws logs filter-log-events --log-group /aws/kms --start-time 1712347200000 --end-time 1712348000000 --filter-pattern "GenerateDataKey" --output json > /tmp/kms_events_1812349999.json` then `aws s3 cp /tmp/kms_events_1812349999.json s3://incidents/1812349999/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control`

kms-bot: Audit export complete. 180 events saved to s3://incidents/1812349999/kms_events_1812349999.json (sha256: ab12...ef).

jordan-sec: good. next: create short-lived deny policy for the key to block GenerateDataKey from that service account and any other non-approved principals. carla, can you add a resource-based deny?

carla-enginfra: adding deny binding now: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding alias/services-data-prod --member="serviceAccount:svc-analytics@redwood-prod" --role="roles/cloudkms.admin" --condition="expr: false"` (note: will add explicit deny via org policy). applying org-level deny for GenerateDataKey from non-approved roles.

maria-sre: status check: revoked SA creds: done. deny policy applied: pending. evidence export: done. key rotation: paused. impacts: a subset of analytics jobs will fail — throttling users notified in #customer-impact.

alex (oncall): starting incident timeline note: 00:12 UTC detection; 00:13 SA disable; 00:15 audit export; 00:18 deny policy applied; 00:22 created incident ticket INC-2026-1812349999 and assigned to jordan-sec and carla-enginfra; 00:30 snapshot of affected storage completed.

jordan-sec: triage: possible causes: leaked service account key, compromised CI runner, or malicious lambda execution environment. next steps: rotate any cached tokens, run container image diff for analytics-worker, check CI logs for token exposures, increase KV cache TTL to avoid reusing old creds.

samir-engr: I'll take CI log check and token rotation. maria-sre, can you own customer comms if production-facing jobs will be affected?

maria-sre: yes, I'll post an update in #customer-impact and prepare a short status for product.

alex (oncall): handing off to daytime oncall at 08:00 UTC: @maria-sre will lead next shift. jordan-sec and carla-enginfra remain on incident SME rotation. please include a runbook section in the ticket for reproducing access pattern and list of keys impacted.

maria-sre: acknowledged. I'll add runbook notes and attach the S3 export. planning a 09:00 post-incident sync with infra and sec.

jordan-sec: leave forensic artifacts as-is. do not rotate key until sec signs off on rekey plan. we may revoke old key with grace period for re-encryption.

alex (oncall): adding final note: created a preserve snapshot of the analytics container image and uploaded to gcr://incidents-preserve/analytics-worker:preserve-1812349999. handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
